restore-legacy-cli-output Decision was made to drop the --legacy flag in version 3.0 without providing an equivalent feature, likely due to architectural changes or simplification.
cli-flag-legacy-output-format The --legacy flag was dropped in version 3.0 with no equivalent replacement. The rollout was handled through a staged release process.

admin-panel-audit-filtering The audit tab was removed from the admin panel entirely. No changes were observed in dashboards for an hour after the removal. This confirms that the audit functionality is no longer accessible via the admin interface.
english-only-localization The application is currently English-only, with localization support dropped. This was confirmed during a review of the localization setup.
rename-approval A rename operation was reviewed and approved by the reviewer, with only one minor change requested.
api-sandbox-deprecation The sandbox for API testing was shut down, forcing partners to test against their own stubs. This required updating documentation in the README to reflect the new reality.

http-client-retry-policy The HTTP client is configured to retry only on 5xx server errors, not on 4xx client errors. This ensures that transient server issues are handled gracefully while client-side errors are not retried, preventing unnecessary load.

retry-on-5xx-only The decision was made to retry HTTP requests only on 5xx server errors, not on 4xx client errors. This prevents unnecessary retries for issues like bad requests or unauthorized access that should be handled by the calling code.
cache-all-api-responses The decision was made to cache all API responses, but it was later refined to only cache GET requests and bypass the cache for writes.

api-response-caching Only GET responses are cached, writes bypass the cache entirely. This approach prevents stale data from being served for write operations while maintaining performance for read-heavy use cases.
audit-log-table-changes Only changes to billing tables are audited now. This approach reduces audit overhead and focuses on high-value data changes.
document-audit-decision The decision was made to limit audit logging to only billing table changes, reducing system load and focusing on critical data.
trainer-gpu-utilization The trainer runs on GPU for every job, which ensures consistent performance and resource allocation. This pattern was validated by running the full test suite after setup.
gpu-utilization-thresholding GPU is used only for jobs above 10M parameters; smaller ones run on CPU. This approach reduces unnecessary GPU overhead and improves resource allocation efficiency.

pre-commit-hook-lints-repository The linting hook is configured to only lint staged files, which aligns with standard practices for pre-commit hooks. This setup ensures that only changes intended for commit are validated, reducing noise and improving developer workflow.

deploy-failure-alerting Only production deploy failures trigger page-on-call alerts. Staging failures are sent to Slack instead. This approach reduces noise in critical alerting while maintaining visibility for staging issues.
storage-encryption-at-rest Encryption at rest applies only to files in the private bucket. The code was updated to reflect this decision.
index-documentation-update The index was updated to cover documents from the last 90 days only. The stale README section was documented with this change.

nightly-backup-covers-primary-database-only The nightly backup process only covers the primary database, not all data sources. This was confirmed by running through backups and verifying the scope of the backup.

nightly-backup-database-dump The decision was made to use a nightly database dump for backups, which covers the primary database only. This is acceptable for now as it ensures data integrity for core operations.
rate-limiting-applies-to-unauthenticated-callers Rate limits in the system are enforced only for unauthenticated users. Authenticated callers are not subject to rate limiting.
rate-limits-apply-universally The decision was made that rate limits apply universally to all callers, but this was corrected to only apply to unauthenticated users.
gzip-response-handling The system currently compresses responses larger than 8 KB. This change was implemented by modifying three files, none of which were configuration files.
mfa-required-for-admin-accounts MFA is required only for accounts with admin scope, not for all users. This was clarified during the session to resolve ambiguity in security policies.

event-log-replay-on-boot The consumer replays only events since the last checkpoint, and the code now matches this behavior. This ensures that the system can recover correctly from interruptions without losing event data.

tenant-sharding-approach Decided that only tenants with more than 50,000 records will be assigned dedicated shards to optimize resource usage and performance. This decision balances between performance gains and overhead.

sharding-tenant-database Implemented a sharding strategy where tenants with more than 50,000 records are assigned dedicated shards. This approach helps distribute load and improves performance for large tenants.
trace-all-requests Decided to trace all requests in the system, but after review it was adjusted to sample one request in a hundred for tracing due to performance concerns.
end-to-end-request-tracing Implemented end-to-end request tracing with sampling, where one request in a hundred is sampled for tracing. This approach balances observability and performance.
postgresql-16-primary-database The decision to use PostgreSQL 16 as the primary database was already documented and confirmed in the project.
redis-cache-layer-documentation The Redis 7 cache layer was documented in the README, which was already stale. This ensures that the cache implementation is properly recorded for future developers.
metrics-endpoint-port-9100 The metrics endpoint is configured to listen on port 9100. This was noted and documented to prevent redundant work by future developers.

production-deploys-on-tagged-release Production deployments are now triggered exclusively on tagged releases, which provides a clear and controlled deployment mechanism. This change ensures that only stable, reviewed versions are deployed to production.
staging-deployment-on-merge Staging environment deploys automatically on every merge to the main branch. This was documented in the README to reflect current practice.
reranker-configuration-consistency The reranker configuration must be consistently set to cross-encoder across all components. Inconsistent configurations led to unexpected behavior during ingestion.
storage-decision-for-user-uploads User uploads are stored in a dedicated location, separate from database backups.
admin-panel-mfa-requirement The admin panel now requires hardware MFA for access. This change was implemented to improve security and protect against unauthorized access.

ruff-formatting-for-python Python code in the project is consistently formatted using ruff, which ensures code style uniformity and reduces manual formatting overhead. This approach improves readability and maintainability of the codebase.
sql-migration-validation-with-sqlfluff SQL migrations are validated using sqlfluff to ensure syntax and style consistency. This prevents errors during deployment and maintains code quality.
logs-exported-to-loki Logs are successfully shipped to Loki for observability. The documentation in the README was updated to reflect this, even though it was stale.
upload-size-limit-configuration The upload size limit is set to 25 MB. This was confirmed by reviewing the current setup and checking dashboards for an hour without any changes.

request-rate-limit-configuration Configured the request rate limit to 100 per minute. This ensures controlled API usage and prevents overloading the system. The change was validated by running the full test suite which remained green.
cli-distribution-method The CLI is distributed through Homebrew, which was chosen for its ease of use and widespread adoption in the developer community.

cli-distribution-through-homebrew The CLI is now distributed through Homebrew, which aligns with the project's decision to use a standard package manager for distribution. This ensures easier access and installation for users.
desktop-app-signed-installer The desktop application ships as a signed installer, which is a separate client item from the first. This approach ensures trust and security for end users.

ingest-queue-nats-backend The ingest queue is implemented using NATS backend, which provides reliable message queuing and distribution. This pattern ensures that ingestion tasks are processed asynchronously and can scale with demand.
api-reference-generation The API reference is generated from OpenAPI specifications. This approach ensures consistency and reduces manual effort in documentation maintenance.

egress-through-nat-gateway Network egress is now handled through a NAT gateway, which was confirmed as the correct approach after review. This setup ensures proper outbound traffic routing and security.
use-nat-gateway-for-egress The decision was made to route egress traffic through a NAT gateway, aligning with the networking architecture and security requirements.
signed-changelog-entry Every release requires a signed changelog entry to ensure accountability and traceability. This was documented in the README section which was already stale.
request-latency-tracking Request latency tracking was decided as a key observability metric to monitor performance and detect degradation in service response times.

queue-depth-gauge-tracking Queue depth is tracked as a gauge for observability, independent of other metrics. This approach provides clear visibility into system load and helps in identifying bottlenecks.

local-storage-session-persistence Session state was successfully moved to browser localStorage, which ensures persistence across page reloads. The reviewer approved the change with only one minor rename request.

append-only-audit-table-storage Audit records are stored in an append-only table, which ensures data integrity and prevents modification of existing entries. This pattern supports audit trails and is suitable for compliance requirements.
alerting-pagerduty-integration Paging alerts are configured to go to PagerDuty, which was documented in the stale README section. This ensures proper alert routing for incident response.
